note: Deliberately legacy-only (no `cells`): this is a PRECISION twin of ts-http-fetch, not a new recall cell — typescript/http_client is already measured there. A single-repo React SPA that both navigates to /dashboard (react-router) and fetches /dashboard. The react-router ROUTE is a browser navigation target, but index_route_node's legacy `<METHOD> <path>` branch cannot tell it from a Spring/Express server route, so the same-repo fetch pairs to the app's own navigation table and HttpStackResolver emits a false HTTP_CALLS edge (a blast_radius carry edge and a weight-5.0 PPR edge). A3.4 marks client-router ROUTEs with an ORIGIN `provenance: nav_route` cell and skips them when building the route index. Both nodes must survive — only the pairing dies.

expect_nodes.name: GET /dashboard
expect_nodes.note: react-router nav route — still a node ('where is /dashboard rendered?' is a real query), just not an HTTP target

forbid.note: THE BUG: a browser navigation target is not a server endpoint; nothing in this SPA may pair. Matched on the endpoint's qname and the nav ROUTE's name, since forbid matches EXACTLY (both nodes share the display name 'GET /dashboard').
